- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7–14 day window and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out forecast curve using 5-day moving average of true values if sentiment volatility > 0.2.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is near recent mean, model often drifts toward extremes; anchor forecast to 3–5 day moving average of historical price range.
